about: Learning and language objectives per lesson, copied verbatim from the first page of each class packet (Lesson_planning/a2_<lesson>.pdf). The Desk shows the current lesson's entry on the desktop so an observer can read it from the back of the room. A lesson with no entry shows nothing; never invent an objective.

mathObjectives: Identify key features of a graph of a function, including the intercepts, positive and negative intervals, and areas where the function is increasing or decreasing.
1-1.languageObjective: Students will explain key features of functions, provided pre-taught vocabulary, the three-reads strategy, and structured student-talk time.
1-1.essentialQuestion: How do key features help you understand functions and their graphs?

mathObjectives: Graph a transformed function by identifying the effect on the graph of replacing f(x) by f(x) + k, kf(x), f(kx), and f(x + k) for specific values of k.
Write an equation of a transformed function.
Relate the domain of a function to its graph and the real-world situation it describes.
1-2.languageObjective: Students will explain transformations of functions, provided pre-taught vocabulary, the three-reads strategy, and structured student-talk time.
1-2.essentialQuestion: How do the values a, b, h, and k in a·f(b(x − h)) + k transform the graph of a parent function, f(x)?
